title: Team and ops
purpose: When work is slipping, a person is overloaded or a vendor is not doing what we pay for, open Team and ops to see who owns what, what is late and what it costs, and put it back on track.
fires: the founder's head as the only task list, the Friday chase on Slack, the vendor's own monthly report, the unread warehouse invoice, and the habit of hiring when it feels busy.
not_for: a solo founder with no staff, vendors or freelancers yet, or a team that only wants a task board.

jobs.job: When I am working 70 hour weeks and still the bottleneck on every decision, show me which work others can own and who should own it, so I get 10 hours back for the calls only I can make
jobs.circumstance: a Sunday night, the founder's inbox has 40 threads waiting on them, 3 people are blocked, a launch slips again

progress.functional: see every recurring task, who does it now, and which ones can move to a named owner
progress.emotional: stop feeling that the business stops when I stop
progress.social: look like a leader to the team, not the person everyone waits on

jobs.hire_today: the founder's own head, a coach or a friend's advice, or a virtual assistant with no clear list
jobs.fire: the founder as the task list and the habit of doing it myself because it is faster

forces.push: growth stops at the founder's hours
forces.pull: a list of work to hand off, each with an owner and a check
forces.habit: it is faster if I do it
forces.anxiety: what if the work is done badly and I pay for it later

jobs.little_hire: every Monday, and whenever the founder's week runs over 60 hours

watch.metric: founder hours a week on tasks with another named owner possible, logged weekly
watch.source: task and decision log in the brand brain

drives.metric: decisions waiting on the founder over 48 hours, weekly

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 70 hour weeks, 18 decisions waiting on the founder. After: 12 recurring tasks moved to 3 owners, 58 hour weeks, 4 decisions waiting.
jobs.not_for: a solo founder with no one yet to hand work to

jobs.job: When my operations manager gives 2 weeks notice, show me what only they know and hold, logins, supplier contacts, steps, so the business does not stop when they leave
jobs.circumstance: a resignation on a Friday, 10 working days left, nobody else has run a reorder, a warehouse call or the payroll file

progress.functional: list every login, contact, file and task that sits with one person, and who takes each
progress.emotional: stop the panic that the business will freeze
progress.social: hand over calmly in front of the team and suppliers

jobs.hire_today: the founder asking the leaver to write it all down, or nothing until something breaks
jobs.fire: the last-week brain dump and the habit of trusting one person with everything

forces.push: orders, ads or payments stop when the one person is gone
forces.pull: a single-person risk list with a named backup for each item
forces.anxiety: what if the leaver holds back or the list is incomplete

jobs.little_hire: every quarter, and the day anyone gives notice

watch.metric: critical logins, contacts and tasks with only one person able to do them, quarterly
watch.source: access list, SOP register and supplier list in the brand brain

drives.metric: days of disruption after a person leaves

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 14 critical items held by one person. After: 2 within 30 days, each with a backup who has done it once.
jobs.not_for: a team where every role already has a trained backup

jobs.job: When tickets about late orders jump during a sale, tell me if the warehouse missed its ship time and by how much, so I hold them to the contract and get credits
jobs.circumstance: a sale week, customers asking where orders are, the warehouse partner says all is fine

progress.functional: know orders shipped on time against the contract, by day, and the credit owed
progress.emotional: stop feeling helpless against the warehouse
progress.social: hold a firm, fair conversation backed by facts

jobs.hire_today: an operations lead checking by hand, the warehouse's own report, or nothing
jobs.fire: the warehouse's self-reported numbers and the habit of taking their word

forces.push: late orders bring tickets, refunds and lost repeat buyers
forces.pull: on-time rate against the contract with credits owed
forces.habit: the warehouse reports its own numbers
forces.anxiety: what if pushing sours a partner we cannot easily replace

watch.metric: orders shipped within the contract ship time, weekly
watch.source: store orders and warehouse ship times

drives.metric: tickets about late orders per 100 orders, weekly

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 82 percent on time against a 98 percent promise, no credits claimed. After: 96 percent within 6 weeks, $3,200 credited.
jobs.not_for: a brand that ships its own orders in-house

jobs.job: When I want to take 2 weeks off without the store falling over, show me what would stop without me and who covers each part, so I can leave and actually switch off
jobs.circumstance: a family holiday booked, the founder has not had a week off in 2 years, the team is capable but unsure

progress.functional: list what only the founder does, and a named cover and rule for each
progress.emotional: stop the guilt and dread of leaving
progress.social: show the family and team the business runs without me

jobs.hire_today: nothing, because the founder just does not take time off
jobs.fire: the phone on the beach and the habit of never leaving

forces.push: burnout, and a business worth less because it needs one person
forces.pull: a cover plan with owners, limits and a way to reach me only for real emergencies
forces.anxiety: what if something big breaks while I am away

jobs.little_hire: before every break, and once a quarter as a drill

watch.metric: founder-only tasks with a named cover, before each break
watch.source: task and decision log in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 0 weeks off in 2 years. After: 2 weeks away with 3 interruptions, none urgent.
jobs.not_for: a founder who already takes regular time off without trouble

jobs.job: When a reorder is missed because 2 people each thought the other had it, give every recurring job one named owner, so it does not happen again

jobs.fire: the blame meeting and the habit of shared ownership

forces.push: things that 2 people own nobody owns

forces.habit: we are a small team, we all pitch in
forces.anxiety: what if people feel boxed in

jobs.little_hire: monthly, and after anything is dropped

watch.metric: recurring jobs with exactly one named owner, monthly
watch.source: ownership chart in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 2 missed reorders this year from shared ownership. After: every recurring job has one owner, 0 misses.
jobs.not_for: a solo founder who owns everything

forces.push: a late run means stockouts and rush freight

forces.anxiety: what if pushing the supplier slows them further

watch.source: purchase order tracker in the brand brain

drives.metric: days late for stock arrival, per order
